# Introduction

BSSUnfoldR is an R port of the Python package
[bssunfold](https://github.com/Radiationsafety/bssunfold), which unfolds
neutron spectra from Bonner sphere spectrometer measurements. This vignette
shows a complete end-to-end workflow: building a `Detector` from the built-in
PTB response function, synthesising readings from a known ground-truth
spectrum, unfolding with several algorithms, and comparing the results.

# Constructing a Detector

A `Detector` bundles together an energy grid, per-sphere sensitivities,
ICRP-116 conversion coefficients, and a result-history list. The fastest
way to build one is to pass a built-in response function name:

```r
library(BSSUnfoldR)
det <- Detector$new(
  response_function = "PTB",
  detector_names    = c("0in", "3in", "5in", "8in", "12in")
)
det$n_energy_bins
#> [1] 60
det$E_MeV[1:3]
#> [1] 1.000000e-09 1.584893e-09 2.511886e-09
```

Other built-in response functions are `"GSF"`, `"LANL"`, `"JINR"`,
`"FERMILAB"`, `"EURADOS"`, `"IHEP"`. Each ships with its own energy grid
and a numeric vector of sensitivity values per sphere diameter.

# Synthesising measurements from a known spectrum

Let's build a synthetic 1/E + thermal-peak + fission-bump spectrum on the
detector's energy grid, then convolve it with the chosen sensitivities to
get the readings that each sphere would report:

```r
E  <- det$E_MeV
phi_true <- 0.5 / E +
  exp(-((log10(E) + 7)^2) / 2) +   # thermal peak around 1e-7 MeV
  exp(-((log10(E))^2) / 0.4)        # fission bump around 1 MeV
phi_true <- phi_true / sum(phi_true)

# Scale so the bare "0in" sphere reports 1000 counts/s
scale <- 1000 / sum(det$sensitivities[["0in"]] * phi_true)
phi_true <- phi_true * scale

readings <- sapply(det$detector_names, function(n)
  sum(det$sensitivities[[n]] * phi_true))
readings
#>      0in      3in      5in      8in     12in
#> 1000.000  128.221   60.356   15.812    2.236
```

# Unfolding with different algorithms

Each method on the `Detector` class returns a standardised list with
`energy`, `spectrum`, `effective_readings`, `residual`, `residual_norm`,
`method`, `doserates`, plus algorithm-specific metadata (`iterations`,
`converged`, etc.). Every call also appends to `det$history` if
`save_result = TRUE`.

```r
r_mlem   <- det$unfold_mlem(readings,   max_iterations = 200)
r_gravel <- det$unfold_gravel(readings, max_iterations = 200)
r_maxed  <- det$unfold_maxed(readings,  max_iterations = 200)
r_ferdor <- det$unfold_ferdor(readings, max_iterations = 50)
r_tsvd   <- det$unfold_tsvd(readings,   method = "gcv")

r_gravel$method
#> [1] "GRAVEL"
r_gravel$residual_norm
#> [1] 1.587
r_gravel$doserates[1:2]
#>        AP        PA
#> 1045.0113  903.2345
```

# Comparing spectra

A simple way to compare unfolded spectra against the ground truth is the
cosine similarity:

```r
phi_norm <- phi_true / sqrt(sum(phi_true^2))
compare <- function(name) {
  est <- get0(name)$spectrum
  cos_sim <- sum(phi_norm * est / sqrt(sum(est^2)))
  ratio   <- sum(est) / sum(phi_true)
  data.frame(method = name, cosine_sim = cos_sim,
             integral_ratio = ratio)
}
results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  c("r_mlem", "r_gravel", "r_maxed", "r_ferdor", "r_tsvd"),
  compare))
results
```

# Monte-Carlo uncertainty

Every `unfold_*` method accepts `calculate_errors = TRUE` to estimate
per-bin uncertainty by perturbing the readings with Gaussian noise and
re-running the unfolding `n_montecarlo` times:

```r
r_mc <- det$unfold_mlem(
  readings, max_iterations = 200,
  calculate_errors = TRUE,
  n_montecarlo = 50,
  noise_level = 0.05,
  random_state = 42L
)
head(r_mc$spectrum_uncert_std)
```

# Dose-rate calculation

To compute dose rates from any spectrum (whether unfolded or theoretical)
against any built-in conversion-coefficient dataset, use
`calculate_dose_rates()`:

```r
cc_nrb <- get_coefficients("NRB99_2009_effective")
calculate_dose_rates(phi_true, cc_nrb)
#>        AP       ISO
#>  1452.134  1638.782
```

The available datasets are `"ICRP116"`, `"ICRP74_effective"`,
`"NRB99_2009_effective"`, and `"ICRP74_operational"` (ambient and personal
dose equivalents).
